study_families.study_label: MoTrPAC Pre-COVID Sedentary Adult Cohort – Baseline Acute Exercise Bout (EE/RE/CON)
study_families.design: Three-arm parallel-group randomized study (site-stratified block randomization to endurance exercise [EE], resistance exercise [RE], or non-exercise control [CON]); acute-bout sub-study nested within the larger MoTrPAC 12-week training RCT.
study_families.training_load: This report analyzes only the pre-training baseline acute bout; 44/175 participants later completed a post-12-week-training acute bout, but those data are not analyzed here due to small sample size and potential confounding (p.21 'Post training intervention data').
study_families.cointerventions: Pre-test standardization: participants instructed to avoid COX-inhibitors, biotin, caffeine, alcohol, exercise, and to standardize final nutrition before the acute test (p.20 Biospecimen Collection).
study_families.study_notes: Multicenter MoTrPAC Consortium, 10 clinical sites; IRB JHMIRB5 (approval 2019-05-06). Enrollment suspended March 2020 (COVID-19 pandemic), limiting this report to 175/176 pre-COVID baseline participants with ≥1 biospecimen; the full post-suspension cohort (planned >1500) is reported in a future main MoTrPAC study (p.19 STAR Methods IRB; p.57 Statistical limitations).

reports.inclusion_reason: Identifiable single acute exercise bout (40-min cycling EE or multi-exercise RE circuit) with a pre-exercise baseline and multiple post-cessation blood samples (10 min to 24 h) plus a non-exercise control arm, in generally healthy sedentary adults (mean age 41±15 y) (p.5-6 Results 'Research design and clinical characteristics'; p.19-21 STAR Methods 'Acute Exercise Intervention' and 'Biospecimen Collection').
reports.reviewer_notes: Preprint (bioRxiv v2, not peer-reviewed) → charted here per manual but routed to the frontier register, never the peer-reviewed core denominator (v2 contract 'Sources' paragraph; v3 contract 2.5). Immune content is one of several co-equal aims (abstract lists 'immune cell responses' alongside lipid metabolism and tissue repair/angiogenesis), not the paper's sole focus, so reports.immune_link uses the 'biofluid_omics_with_immune_objective...' + 'immune_cell_omics' combination rather than 'direct_immune_cell_or_count'. Exact per-timepoint sample sizes are not reported in the accessible text/supplements (deferred to an unpublished companion 'Multi-Omic Landscape' manuscript, p.6, p.21, p.37). No screening decision fields exist yet for this pilot item (pilot_manifest.json reviewer decisions are still null as of 2026-10-05); per contract §5 this AI extraction does not assign eligibility.
reports.author_stated_use: "...provide a new resource for the scientific community" / mechanistic discovery resource characterizing exercise-induced biochemical changes and candidate exerkines; not framed as a clinical or field-deployable monitoring tool (Abstract, p.3; Discussion p.18 'we provide all of these data in an accessible resource for the broader scientific and medical communities').
author_window_interpretation_locator: p.14-17 Results 'Whole blood transcriptional responses to acute exercise' and 'Resistance exercise leads to greater innate immune cellular responses' describe transient NK/CD8+ T-cell and granulocyte mobilization with return to baseline by 30 min-3.5 h, without using 'open window', 'immunosuppression', 'susceptibility' or 'redistribution' terminology anywhere in the text (checked Results, Discussion, Abstract).

cohorts.cohort_label: MoTrPAC pre-COVID sedentary adult baseline cohort (EE/RE/CON arms)
cohorts.baseline_health: Healthy but sedentary adults; screened to confirm eligibility and medical clearance for randomization (questionnaires, anthropometrics, resting HR/BP, fasted blood panel, CPET, strength testing); full inclusion/exclusion criteria reported in a companion 'Clinical Landscape' manuscript (in submission, not accessible) (p.19-20 'Participant Characteristics'; p.20 'Participant Assessments').
cohorts.n_recruited: 176 (completed the baseline acute test: EE=66, RE=73, CON=37); 175 (99%) of these had ≥1 biospecimen sample collected and are analyzed in this report.
cohorts.age_sex: Overall mean age 41±15 y; 126 female (72%) / 49 male (28%); mean BMI 26.9±4.0 kg/m² (Table 1, p.63). Platform-specific subsets in Table S1 (p.65-66); sex-stratified characteristics in Table S2 (p.70).
cohorts.training_status: Sedentary at baseline (study inclusion criterion); subsequently randomized to EE or RE 12-week training, or CON (p.5-6 Results; p.19-21 STAR Methods).
cohorts.sport: NA – standardized laboratory exercise modes (cycle ergometry for EE; multi-exercise resistance circuit for RE), not a competitive sport.
cohorts.cohort_notes: Recruited across 10 MoTrPAC clinical sites; per Statistical limitations, 74% of participants with biosamples were randomized at only 2 of the 10 sites, and 74% of participants came from four of the ten sites – a potential generalizability limitation (p.57-58). Enrollment pool is the same recruited cohort underlying all three randomized arms (EE/RE/CON); arm membership captured at the sample_sets level (group_condition), not as separate cohort rows.
cohorts.age_range: NR – only mean±SD given (41±15 y overall; e.g. 43±16 y for the proteomics subset, Table S1); no explicit min-max age range stated in this report.

sample_sets.repeated_sampling: Yes – same participants sampled longitudinally across pre-, during- (EE/CON only) and post-exercise timepoints up to 24 h (p.20-21 'Biospecimen Collection').
sample_sets.pairing_structure: Within-participant paired pre-exercise vs post-exercise design; mixed-effects model with participant ID as random effect (cell-means model for group x timepoint) (p.41-42).
sample_sets.age_sex_stratum: NA – sex/age included as model covariates, not as a stratified sample_set in the main analysis (sex-stratified descriptive characteristics only in Table S2, p.70).
sample_sets.preanalytics: Standardized tissue-specific collection/processing protocols; blood collected into PAXgene tubes for transcriptomics or processed to plasma for proteomics/metabolomics; full collection/processing detail referenced to a companion 'Clinical Landscape' paper (ref 35) (p.20-21).
sample_sets.normalization: Platform-specific: transcriptomics TMM-normalized (edgeR) with batch correction for clinical site, RIN and %UMI duplication via limma::removeBatchEffect; proteomics reported as Olink NPX (log2 relative protein expression), normalized to plate control; metabolomics SERRF + internal-standard drift correction, then median-MAD or log2 normalization (p.33-34, 36-37, 40).
sample_sets.circadian: Participants arrived fasted in the morning and rested supine ≥30 min before the pre-exercise (baseline) collection; clinical site is included as a covariate in all models to help account for site/time-of-day effects (p.20, 43).
sample_sets.missing_data: Exact n for this specific group x platform x timepoint cell is NR in the accessible text/supplements (media-1.xlsx Tables S1-S4; media-2.docx Key Resources Table; supplement-3.pdf duplicate figure legends – none give a timepoint-level n table). Platform-level TOTAL n by group (not timepoint-specific, from Table S1, p.65): CON=37, EE=64, RE=72. Methods 'Missingness' (p.44) states sample sizes per assay/timepoint/group vary due to temporal randomization (participants randomized to a subset of post-exercise timepoints, p.20-21 'Biospecimen Collection') and platform-specific QC exclusions (blood RIN<5 exclusion, 79/1032 samples, p.25; Olink outlier exclusion, 4/378 samples, p.33; metabolomics outlier/missingness filters, p.39-40); minimum 3 paired participants per group-timepoint required for a feature to enter differential analysis (p.44-45).
